title: They won’t hear the Gospel… because you chose comfort.
paragraphs: They won’t hear the Gospel… because you chose comfort.
Silence feels harmless.
But it isn’t.
It’s eternal.
Somewhere right now, someone you know is one breath away from eternity—and they’ve never heard that Jesus Christ died for them.

Not clearly.
Not personally.
Not urgently.
And heaven is not automatic.

Hell is real.
Sin is deadly.
And neutrality… is a decision.
“How will they believe in Him of whom they have not heard?” — Romans 10:14
Let that sit.

You’re not just quiet.
You’re withholding the cure while the disease spreads.
But here’s what we miss…
Evangelism is not about being perfect.
It’s about being rescued.

You don’t need a microphone.
You need a testimony.

You don’t need a stage.
You need surrender.
Because the Gospel is simple:

We sinned.
We rebelled.
We deserved judgment.
But Jesus Christ stepped in—took the wrath, carried the cross, and rose again—so anyone who repents and believes in Him will not perish but have eternal life.

That includes your friend.
Your sibling.
Your coworker.
Yes—that one you keep avoiding.
And that’s where grace walks in.
God is not asking you to save them.
He’s asking you to speak.

To love them enough to risk awkwardness.
To open your mouth even when your voice shakes.
Because eternity is louder than your fear.
So wake up, believer.

Not with guilt—
but with fire.

Not with pressure—
but with purpose.
Someone’s forever may be hanging on your obedience today.
Message someone. Pray for someone. Speak to someone.
And trust that the same Jesus who saved you… is still saving.
From silence to salvation.
Because grace was never meant to be hidden.
